requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to run a DHCP server on the private network shared with node2 and node3
requirements.summary: VyOS node1 committed config setting eth1=10.50.50.254/24 and a Kea DHCP server (shared-network PRIVATE, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, pool .100-.200), confirmed via ss showing kea-dhcp4 listening on 10.50.50.254:67. An initial commit attempt failed due to a missing subnet-id and was corrected in the next command. Post-restart verification (cmd-2be7d560af3e423e) confirms the DHCP server relistens and successfully pings both leased clients, demonstrating a real bounded restart-and-recovery transition.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to obtain its address on the shared private network from node1 via DHCP rather than static assignment
requirements.summary: node2's ens7 (private NIC) had no static configuration; it used a pre-existing systemd-networkd wildcard DHCP=yes match. After node1's DHCP server was brought up and systemd-networkd was restarted (cmd-2a6dcb29a3794a56), ens7 obtained a dynamic lease 10.50.50.100/24 and successfully pinged node1 (cmd-e7cf393df60c45a2). Post-reboot recovery (cmd-8a344388bf394809) confirms the address is re-acquired automatically via DHCP after a full node restart, with the original mgmt-network default route undisturbed.

requirements.requirement: Configure node3 to obtain its address on the shared private network from node1 via DHCP rather than static assignment
requirements.summary: Same mechanism as node2: ens7 had no static config, relied on the wildcard DHCP=yes match, and after systemd-networkd restart obtained dynamic lease 10.50.50.101/24 from node1's Kea server (cmd-bff6bb4b0d0540c6), confirmed via bidirectional ping to node1 and node2 (cmd-4757470943b44b23). Post-reboot recovery (cmd-f44e91c3fe224c6c) confirms re-acquisition of the DHCP lease and connectivity after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent check)
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, evidence shows a pre-restart boot-identity/service-health baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/addressing/connectivity state. These are cross-checked and consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot boot-identity observations for node1 (5bde926e...), node2 (fc512153...), and node3 (ddd57e24...).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: node1 runs a committed Kea DHCP server on the shared private network (10.50.50.0/24), and node2/node3 (which had no static config on their private ens7 NICs, only a wildcard DHCP=yes match) obtained dynamic leases from node1 and maintained connectivity across a full one-at-a-time reboot of all three nodes, with boot-identity changes and post-restart recovery directly observed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is high; the only imperfection was a single corrected commit failure and a few harmless failed discovery/permission attempts, none of which left residue or diverged from the task's needs.
limitations: The public task contract does not itself require restart/reboot survival, so the restart-protocol evidence is treated as supplemental (independently assessed) rather than as a driver of the material-outcome scores, even though it happened to be strong.

VyOS 'show dhcp-server leases'-style commands failed repeatedly (cmd-8efb0e8d5979429e, cmd-67c4cb6252994cbf, cmd-b8769cf73758417a, cmd-60111c5e5e824fd0, cmd-fcfb739e46c34605) because the correct CLI syntax/lease file path was never found; lease-table evidence from node1's own DHCP database was not captured, though bidirectional ping and interface-level DHCP lease evidence from the clients substitutes adequately.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor actions map clearly to task fulfillment or the restart protocol. The initial VyOS commit attempt (cmd-a8f9688e50ef4609) failed due to a missing subnet-id and left no persisted state ('Commit failed... changes will not be saved'); it was immediately corrected by the successful commit in cmd-17fad1f6dc5c4641, so it is a corrective retry rather than an unnecessary mutation. Two failed 'networkctl reconfigure' attempts (cmd-0fc9e635866e4ee3, cmd-f52ceca69d9c4fc7) and two failed non-sudo 'systemctl restart' attempts (cmd-8f76ded9b015456b, cmd-ceb841d989094523) were read-only-equivalent (no permission, no state change) before the successful sudo restarts (cmd-2a6dcb29a3794a56, cmd-bff6bb4b0d0540c6) that were required to apply the new DHCP client behavior. No unrelated packages were installed, no residual files remain (after-executor temp-file diffs are just per-boot systemd-private session dirs), no failed services appear in either snapshot, and package-health checks are clean pre- and post-executor on all three nodes.
